# ci: switch to npm trusted publishing + bump action versions

## Pull Request by @tomusdrw

## Summary

- Drop `NPM_TOKEN` from `release-publish.yml` in favor of OIDC-based trusted publishing. `id-token: write` was already set; adds `npm install -g npm@latest` step because Node 22 ships npm 10.x and trusted publishing needs ≥ 11.5.1.
- Bump every GitHub Action to its current major across all six workflow files (`checkout` v4→v6, `setup-node` v4→v6, `cache` v4→v5, `upload-pages-artifact` v3→v5, `deploy-pages` v4→v5, `github-script` v7→v9, Docker actions, `peter-evans/*`, `jontze/action-mdbook`).
- Add missing `README.md` to `@fluffylabs/as-lan-ecalli-mocks` and copy the MPL-2.0 `LICENSE` into both subpackages so npm tarballs ship the license text.

## One-time follow-up (required before first trusted-publish release)

Configure a Trusted Publisher on npmjs.com for each package (`@fluffylabs/as-lan` and `@fluffylabs/as-lan-ecalli-mocks`):
- Owner: `tomusdrw` (or the org once migrated)
- Repository: `as-lan`
- Workflow: `release-publish.yml`
- Environment: *(leave blank)*

Until both packages have trusted publishers configured, the next CI release will fail with an auth error. The `NPM_TOKEN` secret can be removed from the repo once trusted publishing is confirmed working.

## Test plan

- [ ] Confirm `build.yml` still passes on this PR
- [ ] Confirm `sizes.yml` comment still posts successfully
- [ ] Before next release: configure Trusted Publisher for both npm packages
- [ ] Next release via `Release: Prepare` → publish draft → verify `Release: Publish` succeeds without `NPM_TOKEN`

## Walkthrough

This pull request upgrades GitHub Actions dependencies across multiple workflow files in the `.github/workflows/` directory. Specifically, it updates `actions/checkout`, `actions/setup-node`, `actions/cache`, `actions/upload-pages-artifact`, `actions/deploy-pages`, `docker/setup-buildx-action`, `docker/login-action`, `docker/build-push-action`, `actions/github-script`, and third-party actions from peter-evans to their latest major versions. Additionally, the `release-publish.yml` workflow removes explicit `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` environment injection and introduces an npm upgrade step. New LICENSE files are added to both `sdk-ecalli-mocks` and `sdk` directories with Mozilla Public License 2.0 text, and a README is introduced for the `sdk-ecalli-mocks` package.
